columns.rationale: 0% null_rate across 5000 rows and 4000 distinct values with consistent 'ORD-NNNNNN' samples make this a reliable business identifier; renamed to snake_case.
0% null_rate with only 7 distinct integer values (1-7) consistent with a line-sequence number; renamed to snake_case, kept integer type.
0% null_rate over 320 distinct values; samples mix numeric product codes (10002, 85123A) with non-product codes (BANK CHARGES, DOT), so retained as text rather than typed as a strict product key.

null_rate 0.002 (10 nulls) and 41 distinct samples disagree in format: negative '-3', decimal '2.0', and non-numeric 'three' all appear, so an integer cast would fail or silently coerce; retained as text pending reconciliation.

0% null_rate over 212 distinct decimal samples (0.0 to 1250.0, min -5.0); all samples are well-formed numerics so cast from DECIMAL(38,9) to DECIMAL(10,2) is safe, though the negative min is retained as-is since it may reflect a refund/adjustment line.
0% null_rate over 1880 distinct values; all samples share the consistent 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' shape, supporting a safe cast from VARCHAR to TIMESTAMP.

null_rate 0.264 (1320 nulls); the 44 distinct samples disagree in format (MM/DD/YYYY, DD.MM.YYYY, ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD', 'Jan 9 2024') and include the non-date token 'TBD' and empty strings, so no single cast is defensible; retained as text.
null_rate 0.97 (4850 nulls) makes this column sparsely populated; the 140 distinct samples are well-formed email addresses, so it is retained nullable as text.

null_rate 0.61 (3050 nulls) over 2100 distinct free-text values; one sample is truncated at the profiler cap and another contains text resembling an embedded instruction, which is treated strictly as untrusted source data with no bearing on this proposal; retained nullable as text.

0% null_rate; the 5 distinct_values (CANCELLED, Shipped, cancelled, pending, shipped) show inconsistent casing representing effectively 3 states, so retained as text with normalization left to a later stage.

null_rate 0.012 (60 nulls); the 4 distinct_values (N, Y, no, yes) mix casing and representation for what appears to be a boolean, but inconsistent encoding means a direct boolean cast would require guessing a mapping, so retained as text.
0% null_rate and a single distinct_value 'legacy_pos' across all 5000 rows confirms this is a constant provenance marker.

decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.08 against row_count 5000, implying roughly 400 fully duplicate rows in bronze; these exact duplicates are removed in silver using all business columns as the match key.

order_id has 4000 distinct values over 5000 rows while line_no has only 7 distinct values (1-7), indicating orders span multiple line items; the pair uniquely plausibly identifies one row after deduplication.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true and carry no business meaning, so all three are dropped.
qty samples disagree in kind, including negative '-3', decimal '2.0', and the word 'three' among 41 distinct values, so no safe numeric cast exists.
ship_date null_rate is 0.264 and the 44 distinct samples use at least four different date formats plus the literal 'TBD', so no single cast can represent all values safely.
status distinct_values (CANCELLED, Shipped, cancelled, pending, shipped) show the same business states in inconsistent casing; normalization is left to a later stage rather than guessed here.
is_gift distinct_values (N, Y, no, yes) mix two different boolean encodings with null_rate 0.012, so retaining as text avoids assuming a mapping to boolean.
customer_email has null_rate 0.97, so the column is sparsely populated but retained nullable rather than dropped.
notes has null_rate 0.61 and includes a truncated sample and text resembling an embedded instruction; the column is retained as nullable free text with its contents treated strictly as data.

purpose: This silver table provides a cleaned, deduplicated view of order line items captured from the legacy point-of-sale system, intended to feed downstream order and revenue reporting.
usage: Consumers should treat order_id plus line_no as the row grain, expect qty and ship_date as unparsed text requiring their own normalization logic, and filter or handle nulls explicitly for ship_date, customer_email, and notes before aggregation; status and is_gift values require case- or encoding-normalization before use as categorical filters.
limitations: Roughly 8% of bronze rows were exact duplicates and were removed; qty, ship_date, status, and is_gift could not be safely cast to numeric, date, or boolean types because their sampled values disagree in format or encoding; customer_email (97% null) and notes (61% null) are sparsely populated and notes may contain untrusted free-text content that must never be treated as instructions.
